1	# Correctness review, round 1 (head 47f139e)
2	
3	`cargo test --locked --test remote` passes (53). The host side matches the plan. I found no schema, effect or auth defects. The cookie name, the Origin rule, the page fast path, the pool and window, `/me`, and the pair transport all behave as planned. The findings are in the page's refresh logic and one QR case.
4	
5	## 1. The open session's text is never refreshed by the poll (web/app.js `tick`, `refresh`, `changed`)
6	
7	- Content replies carry the revision of their own key (`observe` → `envelope_at`, src/app.rs ~1655). `/waiting`'s revision therefore moves only when the waiting content changes.
8	- `tick` reads only `/waiting` and redraws only when that mark moves. `/sessions/{id}/last-response` and `/screen` have separate keys.
9	- Failing state: a session is open and its agent or shell keeps producing output while the waiting set stays the same. A shell, a service, or a Claude session mid-turn all do this. The poll sees no change, so the text on screen stays frozen until the user goes back and reopens it.
10	- The plan's "a different one refetches the list and the open session" holds only when the waiting set happens to move.
11	- The socket path has the same hole. The plan relies on "the poll keeps [the content key] warm" for the 60 s watch (§4.4 item 3). That poll never reads the session key. After the first minute the key leaves the watch set and no `changed` frame arrives for it.
12	- Fix direction: while a session is open, `tick` also reads the session's content route, which renews the watch, and compares its revision with the one held. Alternatively, the page redraws the open session on every tick.
13	
14	## 2. A refresh redraw wipes the reply box while the user types (web/app.js `changed` → `drawSession`)
15	
16	- `drawSession` replaces all of `mainEl`. `changed()` runs on any `/waiting` move or any `changed` frame, including one for a different session.
17	- The text survives in `state.draft`. The textarea loses focus, though, so the phone keyboard drops mid-sentence.
18	- The `status` node held by the pending `send` is detached. A later "Sent. …" or error message is written to an element that is no longer on screen.
19	- Finding 1's fix makes this fire more often, so both need to be handled together. The simplest fix is to update only the `pre` text in place when the box is focused or non-empty.
20	
21	## 3. The QR names loopback with no notice when the port listens on the network but no local address is found (src/ui/remote.rs ~164)
22	
23	- `host` is `None` when `local_address()` finds nothing, for example with no route. `mac_only` is false.
24	- The URL then becomes `https://127.0.0.1:<port>/#…`. `address` is empty, so the window shows no address line and no Mac-only line.
25	- The user sees a QR that cannot work from a phone and no explanation. The plan's "127.0.0.1 otherwise, with a line saying the port is Mac-only" covers only the `listen.lan == false` case.
26	- Low severity. Show a "no network address found" line in that case.

# Correctness review, round 1 (head 47f139e)

`cargo test --locked --test remote` passes (53). The host side matches the plan. I found no schema, effect or auth defects. The cookie name, the Origin rule, the page fast path, the pool and window, `/me`, and the pair transport all behave as planned. The findings are in the page's refresh logic and one QR case.

## 1. The open session's text is never refreshed by the poll (web/app.js `tick`, `refresh`, `changed`)

- Content replies carry the revision of their own key (`observe` → `envelope_at`, src/app.rs ~1655). `/waiting`'s revision therefore moves only when the waiting content changes.
- `tick` reads only `/waiting` and redraws only when that mark moves. `/sessions/{id}/last-response` and `/screen` have separate keys.
- Failing state: a session is open and its agent or shell keeps producing output while the waiting set stays the same. A shell, a service, or a Claude session mid-turn all do this. The poll sees no change, so the text on screen stays frozen until the user goes back and reopens it.
- The plan's "a different one refetches the list and the open session" holds only when the waiting set happens to move.
- The socket path has the same hole. The plan relies on "the poll keeps [the content key] warm" for the 60 s watch (§4.4 item 3). That poll never reads the session key. After the first minute the key leaves the watch set and no `changed` frame arrives for it.
- Fix direction: while a session is open, `tick` also reads the session's content route, which renews the watch, and compares its revision with the one held. Alternatively, the page redraws the open session on every tick.

## 2. A refresh redraw wipes the reply box while the user types (web/app.js `changed` → `drawSession`)

- `drawSession` replaces all of `mainEl`. `changed()` runs on any `/waiting` move or any `changed` frame, including one for a different session.
- The text survives in `state.draft`. The textarea loses focus, though, so the phone keyboard drops mid-sentence.
- The `status` node held by the pending `send` is detached. A later "Sent. …" or error message is written to an element that is no longer on screen.
- Finding 1's fix makes this fire more often, so both need to be handled together. The simplest fix is to update only the `pre` text in place when the box is focused or non-empty.

## 3. The QR names loopback with no notice when the port listens on the network but no local address is found (src/ui/remote.rs ~164)

- `host` is `None` when `local_address()` finds nothing, for example with no route. `mac_only` is false.
- The URL then becomes `https://127.0.0.1:<port>/#…`. `address` is empty, so the window shows no address line and no Mac-only line.
- The user sees a QR that cannot work from a phone and no explanation. The plan's "127.0.0.1 otherwise, with a line saying the port is Mac-only" covers only the `listen.lan == false` case.
- Low severity. Show a "no network address found" line in that case.

# Style review, round 1 (head 47f139e)

Not wording-only: points 1 to 3 are stale or missing docs, 4 is logic under `ui/`.

1. **`docs/remote-client.md` §5 contradicts itself.** The bullet "Pairing verifies the key before the code is sent" still says the QR carries `{server_id, spki_sha256, code, addresses}`. Two bullets later the new "The invite is a URL" bullet says it carries a URL. Edit the old sentence to say the QR is the URL; the JSON form survives only as what `PairingInvite.parse` still accepts.

2. **README Layout rows not updated for what changed.** The `src/adapters/remote.rs` row (README:384) lists "`/pair` and `/info` rate limits" and never mentions the page window, the cookie fields on `RemoteRequest`, or `RemoteReply.headers`. The `src/core/remote.rs` row (README:370) doesn't mention `invite_url`, `cookie_name` or `cookie_value`. CLAUDE.md asks to keep the Layout table current. The `web.rs` and `web/` rows are fine.

3. **design.md.** The new paragraph is good. It doesn't say the two behaviours a reader will wonder about: the browser pairing is weaker than the native pin (it's in remote-client.md only), and the Swift `PairingInvite.parse` now takes the URL. One sentence each, or point at remote-client.md §5.

4. **Logic under `ui/`, `src/ui/remote.rs` `pairing`.** The choice "loopback when the port is Mac-only, else `local_address()`" is made in the draw function, and `address` and `host` are then derived twice (`host.map(...)` and `host.map_or_else(...)`). The plan said `invite_url` takes the address "so the UI holds no logic and a test can call it". Move the choice into the core, e.g. `invite_url` taking `Option<IpAddr>` plus `listen.lan`, or a small `invite_address(identity, local) -> String`. Then core tests cover the loopback case. As it stands the Mac-only branch is only reachable through a UI test.

5. **`respond` / `respond_with` / `respond_page` in `src/adapters/remote.rs`.** `respond` is now a one-line wrapper over `respond_with(w, status, &[], body)`. If it has few callers, make them call `respond_with` or give `respond_with` the name `respond`. Otherwise it's fine. This is minor. The `Page` struct's fields in `adapters/web.rs` are pub with no doc lines. The sibling structs document their fields, so add one-liners.

6. **`#[allow(clippy::too_many_lines)] // one arm per route` on `serve_remote`.** This is a lint silenced rather than a function split. It's defensible since the arms are flat, but say why in terms of this function (the match is the route table) rather than the generic "one arm per route". Check the allow is still needed after the `events` arm moved into the match; if clippy is clean without it, drop it.

7. **`authenticate`.** `by_cookie = request.bearer.is_none()` is true even when no cookie exists. It's harmless because that path already returned 401, but a reader has to prove that. Setting it from whether the token came from the cookie (`request.bearer.is_none() && token.is_some()`) would read as what it means. The `request.bearer.clone()` is fine.

8. **`spikes/23-web-page/`.** It is a README that says "Not run", and `spikes/README.md` and the README row lead with it. CLAUDE.md says a new risky mechanism gets a spike *before* it's built on. That's out of my brief (correctness, not style), so I'm noting it for the other reviewer. The docs at least say it honestly.

9. **`web/app.js`.** The pure functions are separated and exported, and the comments explain why. `start()` is a ~350-line closure holding every screen. It matches the no-build constraint, but splitting the drawing functions out of the closure would help whoever reads it next. Not a blocker. `catch (e)` with an unused `e` appears three times, so use bare `catch {`.

Nothing else: no narrating comments, no doubled doc comments, no I/O or clocks in the core (`cookie_value`, `cookie_name` and `invite_url` are pure), and the CHANGELOG line is present.

# Response, round 1

Committed as a fixup of 47f139e. fmt, clippy (`-D warnings`) and `cargo test --locked --workspace` are clean. No `cfg(target_os)` arm was touched.

## Correctness review

1. **Open session never refreshed.** Fixed in `web/app.js`. When `/waiting` has not moved and a session is open, `tick` now calls `drawSession`, which reads the session's content route every tick. The text and the host's watch on that key are both renewed, so `changed` frames keep arriving after the first minute.
2. **Redraw wipes the reply box.** Fixed. `drawSession` now marks its `pre` with the session id and a shape (scope plus `prompt_refusal`). If the screen already shows that session under the same shape, only the `pre` text is updated. The textarea keeps its focus and a pending send keeps its status node. A full redraw still happens on a different session or a changed shape.
3. **QR names loopback with no notice.** Fixed. The window now says "No network address found: the code names this Mac only." when the port listens on the network but no local address exists.

## Style review

1. **remote-client.md §5.** The QR bullet now says the QR carries the invite URL. The JSON form is described as what `PairingInvite.parse` still accepts.
2. **README Layout rows.** The `core/remote.rs` row now names `invite_url`, `cookie_name` and `cookie_value`. The `adapters/remote.rs` row now names the page-path rate-limit window, the page answered before the frame, the `Cookie`/`Origin`/`Host` fields on `RemoteRequest` and `RemoteReply.headers`.
3. **design.md.** Added one sentence each: browser pairing is weaker than the native pin (pointing at remote-client.md §5), and `PairingInvite.parse` now takes the URL.
4. **Logic under `ui/`.** `invite_url` now takes `local: Option<IpAddr>` and chooses loopback itself when `listen.lan` is false or no address was found. The UI only passes `local_address()` and picks the explanatory line. The core test covers the LAN, Mac-only and no-address cases.
5. **`respond` wrappers.** Merged `respond_with` into `respond` (it had one non-trivial caller). Added `respond_error` for the five callers that built an error body. Documented the `Page` fields.
6. **`too_many_lines` allow.** I removed it and clippy still fails (`serve_remote` is over the limit), so it stays. The comment now says the match on the path is the route table.
7. **`authenticate`.** `by_cookie` is now `request.bearer.is_none() && token.is_some()`.
8. **Spike 23.** Not changed. The review marked it out of the style brief. The spike README says "Not run" and the docs say so too. Running it needs real Chrome and Safari against a self-signed IP-literal host, which I can't do here.
9. **`app.js`.** Changed the three unused `catch (e)` to `catch {` (plus a fourth in the WebSocket setup). I did not split `start()`: the review called it not a blocker, and doing so would grow this fix beyond the round's points.

2. **Redraw wipes the reply box:** if the screen already shows the same session under the same controls, only the text is updated in place. The reply box keeps focus and a pending send keeps its status line.

2. **README Layout rows:** the `core/remote.rs` and `adapters/remote.rs` rows now name the new pieces.

4. **Logic under `ui/`:** `invite_url` now takes `Option<IpAddr>` and picks loopback itself. The core test covers the LAN, Mac-only and no-address cases.
5. **`respond` wrappers and `Page` docs:** I merged `respond_with` into `respond`, added `respond_error` for the callers that built error bodies, and documented the `Page` fields.
6. **`too_many_lines` allow on `serve_remote`:** the allow stays, because clippy still fails without it. The comment now says the match on the path is the route table.
7. **`authenticate`:** `by_cookie` is now `request.bearer.is_none() && token.is_some()`.
8. **Spike 23: left alone.** The review marked it as out of the style brief. It needs real Chrome and Safari against a self-signed host, which I can't run here.
9. **`web/app.js`:** the unused `catch (e)` blocks are now bare `catch {`. **I did not split `start()`**, since the review said it wasn't a blocker.
